title: Measure What Matters
author: John Doerr
blurb: Venture capitalist John Doerr explains Objectives and Key Results, or OKRs, a goal-setting method he learned from Andy Grove at Intel in the 1970s and later introduced to a young Google. An objective is what you want to achieve. Key results are the measurable steps that show whether you are getting there. Doerr argues that OKRs give organizations four superpowers. They help teams focus on what matters most, align everyone's work in the open, track progress honestly and stretch toward ambitious goals. Through stories from Intel, Google, YouTube, nonprofits and startups, he shows the system in action. He then pairs OKRs with continuous conversations, feedback and recognition, which replace the dreaded annual review. The message is that ideas are easy, execution is everything, and clear, shared, measurable goals are how good execution happens.

lessons.t: Ideas Are Easy, Execution Is Everything
lessons.b: Most organizations fail not from bad ideas but from poor execution, and Doerr brought OKRs to an early Google to fix exactly that.
An objective says what you want to achieve, and a few measurable key results say how you will know you got there, a method Andy Grove built at Intel.
